description: Master scheduler configuration: how the simulator advances time, how missions/*.json phases, simulation/events.json triggers, and simulation/weather.json presets all layer onto a single simulation clock, and what gets logged.

integration.note: Override via simulation/defaults.json solver block if a mission needs a different step size (e.g. finer resolution for takeoff/landing transients).

phase_sequencing.rule: Phases execute strictly in array order. A phase with duration_s: null runs until a reserve floor in the mission's reserves block is hit (see missions/README.md), then the next phase begins.

event_layering.rule: Events are checked every time_step_s against their trigger condition. Multiple events may fire in the same phase. Failure-injection events persist their effect for the remainder of the run unless a recovery event is explicitly defined.
event_layering.conflict_resolution: If two events modify the same field in the same step, apply in event_library array order and log a warning.

weather_layering.source: simulation/weather.json -> presets{} or mission-embedded weather block
weather_layering.rule: Mission-embedded weather is the baseline for the full run; an environment_change event (see events.json) overrides it from its trigger point onward.

checkpointing.purpose: Allows resuming/inspecting long optimizer runs (Layer 3) without rerunning the full mission from t=0.

output_record_schema.soc: float, 0-1 fraction (matches PRD dashboard contract, not soc_pct)

logging.note: This record schema is intentionally aligned with the dashboard interface contract's mission_profile array (time_min, altitude_m, power_kw, soc) defined in the PRD, so optimizer_mdo.py can export directly without a reshape step. soc here is a 0-1 fraction per the PRD example; states.json uses soc_pct (0-100) internally — convert at the logging boundary, not throughout the codebase.
